skill.name: triaging-issues
skill.description: Triages GitHub issues by classifying priority, checking duplicates, mapping dependencies, assessing quality, and applying selected repository updates through GitHub CLI.
skill.summary: Review, organize, and act on GitHub issues with consistent triage workflows.
skill.author: C0ntr0lledCha0s

security_audit.summary: Static detections for command substitution, subprocess use, device redirection, Markdown fences, and reconnaissance phrases are false positives in context. The scripts still perform repository mutations through GitHub CLI. Bulk changes lack preview guards, and documented option-style calls do not match positional parsing.

remediation.issue: Bulk commands mutate many GitHub issues without a preview or confirmation step.
remediation.suggestion: Add a dry-run default, display the matched issue count and planned changes, then require explicit confirmation before mutations.

remediation.issue: Documented option-style arguments do not match the scripts' positional argument parsing.
remediation.suggestion: Use getopts or document positional syntax, validate issue identifiers, and complete all preflight checks before closing or editing issues.

semantic_findings.title: Bulk Repository Changes Lack a Preview Guard
semantic_findings.description: Batch triage, bulk labeling, and project assignment immediately mutate matching GitHub issues. A broad filter can alter up to 100 issues without confirmation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The functions call gh issue edit and gh project item-add inside loops without a dry-run or interactive confirmation.

semantic_findings.title: Documented Arguments Can Leave Partial Repository Changes
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md documents option-style helper calls, but the shell script parses positional parameters only. Duplicate closure can finish before its malformed follow-up command fails.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation passes --filter and --original flags, while main forwards raw arguments to functions that read fixed positional slots.

content.user_title: Triage GitHub Issues with Clear Priorities
content.value_statement: Unsorted GitHub issues delay decisions and hide duplicates. This skill classifies issues, maps relationships, checks quality, and prepares focused triage actions.
actual_capabilities: Classifies issues by type, priority, scope, and estimated effort.
Searches open issues for possible duplicates using keywords and title comparisons.
Maps referenced issues, blocking language, labels, and dependency relationships.
Checks issue quality using title, description, labels, reproduction details, and environment information.
Can label issue sets, close duplicates, add project items, and generate triage reports through GitHub CLI.
limitations: Requires GitHub CLI authentication, Bash, jq, and Python for the included scripts.
Duplicate detection uses basic keyword and title matching, not semantic or TF-IDF scoring.
Some documented option-style commands conflict with the scripts' positional interfaces.
Batch mutation commands do not provide a dry-run or confirmation step.

use_cases.title: Review Incoming Reports
use_cases.description: Classify new issues, assess completeness, and prepare labels or information requests.

use_cases.title: Organize a Product Backlog
use_cases.description: Identify duplicates, priorities, dependencies, and issues ready for planning.

use_cases.title: Analyze Engineering Blockers
use_cases.description: Map issue relationships and highlight work that unlocks dependent tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Review One Issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Review GitHub issue #{issue_number}. Classify its type and priority, assess its quality, and recommend next steps without changing the repository.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs a structured review of one issue.

prompt_templates.title: Check for Duplicates
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare issue #{issue_number} with related open issues. Rank likely duplicates, explain the evidence, and recommend whether to link or close each candidate.
prompt_templates.scenario: A maintainer wants evidence before resolving a duplicate.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Batch Triage
prompt_templates.prompt: Review issues matching {filter}. Propose labels, priorities, and information requests. Show a dry-run summary and do not modify GitHub.
prompt_templates.scenario: A product manager wants a reviewable batch plan.

prompt_templates.title: Plan from Dependencies
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze open issues for dependencies, duplicates, quality gaps, and priority. Produce a recommended execution order, then request confirmation before any repository changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: An engineering lead needs a dependency-aware triage plan.

output_examples.output: Issue #42 is a high-priority backend bug. It needs environment details and logs before assignment. Issue #38 may be related.

output_examples.input: Find likely duplicates of the authentication timeout report.
output: Issue #38 is the strongest match because it reports the same timeout and component.
Issue #27 concerns login but reports a different failure mode.
Recommendation: verify #38 before closing or linking any issue.

output_examples.input: Summarize dependency blockers in the current backlog.
output_examples.output: Issue #42 blocks two profile tasks and should start first. Issue #50 has no blockers and can proceed in parallel.

best_practices: Review duplicate evidence and reporter context before closing an issue.
Run batch operations as a dry-run and confirm the matched issue set.
Document classification, priority, and relationship decisions in clear repository comments.
anti_patterns: Do not close duplicates using title similarity alone.
Do not run broad mutation filters without reviewing every matched issue.
Do not assign priority or effort without evidence from impact, urgency, and scope.

faq.question: Does this skill change GitHub issues?
faq.answer: Yes. Some helper commands add labels, close duplicates, comment, or add project items.

faq.question: What tools are required?
faq.answer: The scripts require GitHub CLI, Bash, jq, Python, and authenticated repository access.

faq.question: How are duplicates detected?
faq.answer: The included script extracts keywords and compares titles across open issues.

faq.question: Can it process many issues?
faq.answer: Yes. Batch commands support up to 100 matching issues, but they lack built-in preview confirmation.

faq.question: Does it validate issue quality?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks titles, descriptions, labels, reproduction details, issue references, and environment information.

faq.question: Can it map dependencies?
faq.answer: Yes. It extracts issue references, scans blocking language, and generates text or DOT relationship output.
